Camila / Laura — quick read and my suggestions below. Bottom line: we should not agree to a one-way exclusion. As a general matter, asymmetric exclusions materially increase risk (and set a bad precedent). We can offer a tightly scoped exception, with three controls: causation standard, demonstrable proof, and a monetary sub-cap. Proposed redline (sendable to counterparty):

---- PROPOSED REDLINE (excerpt) ----
Section X.Y Excluded Damages: Except for Damages resulting from (i) Redwood’s gross negligence or willful misconduct, (ii) a material breach of Redwood’s security or confidentiality obligations, or (iii) third-party fines or penalties finally adjudicated against Customer that are a direct result of Redwood’s breach of applicable data protection law, the parties agree that neither party shall be liable to the other for consequential, special, incidental, exemplary or punitive damages.

Further, liability for damages permitted under the exceptions above shall be subject to a sub-cap equal to the greater of (A) $2,000,000 or (B) the total fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the applicable Order Form in the preceding 12 months. Any claim relying on an exception must be supported by contemporaneous evidence demonstrating causal connection between Redwood’s conduct and the claimed loss; recovery for indirect downstream reimbursement adjustments shall be limited to amounts actually assessed against the Customer (net of recoveries).

---- end excerpt ----

Rationale: 1) Mutual exclusion preserves symmetry; 2) exceptions address Acme’s real concern (gross negligence/security/data law fines) but with a defined monetary and evidentiary limit; 3) sub-cap makes exposure bounded and insurable.

Operational asks if Acme accepts: require prompt notification, time-bound investigation (90 days), and a cooperation clause for recovery from third parties. Also flag: we should avoid including language that allows recovery for speculative lost profits or multiplier damages.

If Laura signs off, Camila — send the proposed redline and the definition matrix. I can do a terse cover note explaining the approach.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Knock-on loss exclusion — proposed compromise

Jordan — thanks for the patience. We discussed this with legal and want to propose a compromise intended to address Acme’s operational concern while preserving reciprocal protection for both parties:

Proposal (summary):
- Maintain mutual exclusion for consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages.
- Create narrowly defined exceptions for liability arising from: (i) Redwood’s gross negligence or willful misconduct; (ii) a material breach of Redwood’s security obligations resulting in unauthorized access to Customer data; and (iii) third-party fines or penalties finally adjudicated against Customer that are directly attributable to Redwood’s breach of applicable data protection law.
- Any claim under an exception must demonstrate causation with contemporaneous evidence; recovery for downstream reimbursement adjustments will be limited to amounts actually assessed against Acme (net of recoveries).
- Exceptions will be subject to a sub-cap equal to the greater of $2,000,000 or the fees paid by Acme under the applicable Order Form in the prior 12 months.
- Operational requirements: prompt notice, 90-day investigation/cooperation window, and joint forensic review for security events.

Attached are the redline and a short definition matrix that maps examples to the exception language. If Acme prefers a different numeric sub-cap we can consider it in the context of term/volume commitments.

If this looks reasonable, we’re happy to memorialize in a short call with procurement/legal to finalize quickly.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
